senses.gloss: (b. h.; cmp. גשר) [to be well-joined, (cmp. יָפֶה, אֲרִיךְ II),] to be proper, fit, right; to turn out well, to succeed.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Challah 1:1:11">Y. Ḥall. I, 57ᵇ</cite> top <he>החטים שׁכָּשְׁרוּ לשאר וכ׳</he> wheats which are fit for all other meat offerings; ib. 57ᶜ; Sifra Vayikra, N’dabah, ch. XIV, Par. 13; a. fr.—V. <cite ref="K01326"><he>כָּשֵׁר</he> II</cite>.

senses.gloss: (ritual, v. כָּשֵׁר II) to pronounce kasher, to permit.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Chullin 3:2">Ḥull. III, 2</cite> <he>ר׳</he> … <he>מַכְשִׁיר</he> R. pronounces it fit to be eaten, opp. <he>פוסל</he>; a. v. fr.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 6:1">Ab. VI, 1</cite> <he>מַכְשַׁרְתּוֹ להיות וכ׳</he> enables him to be righteous &c.

<cite ref="Chullin 140a">Ḥull. 140ᵃ</cite> <cite ref="M01442"><he>מַכְשִׁיר</he></cite> an offering which makes fit for admission to the Temple or eating sacred food, contrad. to <he>מכפר</he> an offering which procures atonement; <cite ref="Kiddushin 57a">Kidd. 57ᵃ</cite>, a. e.—

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 42b:1-11">Snh. 42ᵇ</cite> <he>הוצא</he> … <he>מכשיר ומכפר</he> ‘the carrying outside of the camp’ (<cite ref="Leviticus 4:12">Lev. IV, 12</cite>; <cite ref="Leviticus 4:21">21</cite>) makes the act legal and procures atonement; <cite ref="Leviticus 4:21">ib.</cite> <he>מכשיר ממכשיר עדיף ליה</he> the analogy between one fitting act and another is preferred.—
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Kamma 1:2">B. Kam. I, 2</cite> <he>הִכְשַׁרְתִּי את נזקו</he> I have prepared (am responsible for) the damage, v. <cite ref="H00231"><he>חוּב</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Kamma 1:2">Ib.</cite> <he>הכשרתי</he> (<cite ref="B00000"><he>ב</he></cite>)<he>מקצת נזקו וכ׳</he> wherever I am the partial cause of a damage (e.g. by completing a pit to its legally indictable depth), I am as responsible as if I had been the entire author.

Gen. R. s. 56 the slaughtering knife is called מַאֲכֶלֶת (causing the eating) לפי שׁמַכְשֶׁרֶת את האוכלים (not שמכשר) because it makes the food fit for eating.—Esp. (with or without לקבל טומאה) to make an object fit for levitical uncleanness (v.

<cite ref="Chullin 35b:9">Ḥull. 35ᵇ</cite> <he>וכי הדם מַכְשִׁיר … מַכְשֶׁרֶת</he> is it the blood (as a liquid) which fits the meat for uncleanness?; is it not rather the slaughtering (because it makes it ‘an eatable’)?—
<cite ref="Chullin 33a:13">Ib. 33ᵃ</cite> <he>חיבת הקדש מַכְשַׁרְתָּן</he>, v. <cite ref="H00016"><he>חִבָּה</he></cite>; <cite ref="Chullin 36b:13">ib. 36ᵇ</cite> <he>מַכְשַׁרְתָּהּ</he>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Makhshirin 6:6">Makhsh. VI, 6</cite>. Y. Gitt. I, 43ᶜ <he>על מי בצים שאינן מַכְשִׁירִין</he> that the liquid of eggs does not fit for uncleanness; Y. Shebi. VI, 36ᶜ top <he>שאין כשירין</he> (corr. acc.); a. v. fr.—V. <cite ref="E00526"><he>הֶכְשֵׁר</he></cite>, <cite ref="M01442"><he>מַכְשִׁירִין</he></cite>.

senses.gloss: to be made fit; to be pronounced fit; to be prepared; to be fitted for levitical uncleanness.
units: <cite ref="Yoma 50a">Yoma 50ᵃ</cite> <he>במה ה׳ אהרן וכ׳</he> through what act is Aaron (a high priest) made fit to enter &c.?—
<cite ref="Shabbat 76a:1">Sabb. 76ᵃ</cite> <he>כל שאינו כשר … וה׳ לזה וכ׳</he> that which is not fit for preservation but appeared fit to this man, and he did preserve it.
<cite ref="Chullin 22b:2">Ḥull. 22ᵇ</cite> <he>הוּכְשְׁרוּ</he> are pronounced fit for sacrifices.

<cite ref="Mishnah Chullin 2:5">Ib. II, 5</cite> <he>הוכשרו בדם</he> they became fit for uncleanness through the blood (flowing out at killing); <he>ה׳ בשחיטה</he> they became fit through the act of slaughtering (v. supra); a. v. fr.—[Y. Keth. XII, 35ᵃ <he>מכושר</he>, read: <he>מב׳</he>, v. <cite ref="B01368"><he>בָּשַׂר</he></cite>.]

senses.gloss: to adapt one’s self, to work with zeal and conscientiousness.
units: <cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 5:11:5">Koh. R. to V, 11</cite> <he>מִתְכַּשֵּׁר במלאכתו וכ׳</he> more skilled and zealous in his work than &c. (cmp. <cite ref="G00703"><he>זָרִיז</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 9">Gen. R. s. 9</cite>; a. e.
